prompt: Which of the following best describes market equilibrium?

options.label: A
options.text: The price at which all sellers earn identical producer surplus

options.label: B
options.text: The quantity at which every buyer has the same willingness to pay

options.label: C
options.text: The price at which consumer surplus equals producer surplus

options.label: D
options.text: The quantity at which demand and supply have equal slopes

options.label: E
options.text: The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied

explanation: Equilibrium is the price at which consumers' planned purchases equal producers' planned sales. Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

prompt: At the equilibrium price in a perfectly competitive market,

options.label: A
options.text: The benefit to buyers equals the benefit to sellers

options.label: B
options.text: The demand curve has the same slope as supply

options.label: C
options.text: The quantity buyers want equals the quantity sellers offer

options.label: D
options.text: Each seller incurs the same cost per unit

options.label: E
options.text: Each buyer values the good by the same amount

explanation: The market clears when the quantity buyers want exactly matches the quantity sellers offer.

prompt: Which of the following is true at a market-clearing price?

options.label: A
options.text: Consumer surplus must equal producer surplus in the market

options.label: B
options.text: Every producer is willing to sell at the same cost

options.label: C
options.text: Neither a shortage nor a surplus

options.label: D
options.text: Every consumer is willing to buy the same quantity

options.label: E
options.text: The highest-cost seller receives the greatest producer surplus

explanation: A market-clearing price equates quantity demanded and supplied. Neither excess demand nor excess supply remains.

prompt: The equilibrium quantity is the quantity

options.label: A
options.text: Buyers purchase and sellers sell at the equilibrium price

options.label: B
options.text: For which consumer surplus equals producer surplus

options.label: C
options.text: Sellers would offer at the demand curve’s intercept

options.label: D
options.text: Buyers would purchase if the good had a price of zero

options.label: E
options.text: For which the demand and supply slopes are equal

explanation: At equilibrium, buyers and sellers choose the same quantity. This common amount is the equilibrium quantity traded.

prompt: Consumer surplus from one unit equals

options.label: A
options.text: The buyer’s willingness to pay minus the seller’s revenue

options.label: B
options.text: The price received minus the seller’s cost

options.label: C
options.text: The price paid minus the buyer’s willingness to pay

options.label: D
options.text: The buyer’s willingness to pay minus the price paid

options.label: E
options.text: The seller’s cost minus the price received

explanation: Consumer surplus is the buyer's willingness to pay minus the actual price. It measures the net benefit from purchasing.

prompt: Based on the figure below, market equilibrium occurs

options.label: A
options.text: Where demand and supply intersect at point E

options.label: B
options.text: Where supply reaches its quantity-axis intercept

options.label: C
options.text: Where demand lies above supply at the same quantity

options.label: D
options.text: Where demand reaches its price-axis intercept

options.label: E
options.text: Where supply lies below demand at the same quantity

explanation: Demand and supply meet at E. Both curves give quantity Qe at price Pe, identifying equilibrium.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity is on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping demand curve D and an upward-sloping supply curve S intersect at point E. Dashed guides from E identify equilibrium price Pe and equilibrium quantity Qe.

graphScenes.caption: Schematic; only labeled numbers are quantitative

prompt: A buyer’s willingness to pay is best interpreted as

options.label: A
options.text: The maximum amount the buyer would pay for a unit

options.label: B
options.text: The difference between equilibrium price and seller cost

options.label: C
options.text: The total producer surplus generated by one unit

options.label: D
options.text: The minimum amount a seller would accept for a unit

options.label: E
options.text: The market price received by every seller of the good

explanation: Willingness to pay is the maximum amount a buyer values a unit. Paying less than this amount creates consumer surplus.

prompt: Producer surplus from one unit equals

options.label: A
options.text: The price received minus the seller’s cost

options.label: B
options.text: The price paid minus the buyer’s willingness to pay

options.label: C
options.text: The buyer’s willingness to pay minus the price paid

options.label: D
options.text: The seller’s revenue minus the buyer’s valuation

options.label: E
options.text: The seller’s cost minus the price received

explanation: Producer surplus is the price received minus the unit's cost or minimum acceptable price. It measures the seller's gain from the trade.

prompt: On a supply curve, a seller’s minimum acceptable price for a unit reflects the seller’s

options.label: A
options.text: Total revenue from all units

options.label: B
options.text: Cost of supplying that unit

options.label: C
options.text: Consumer surplus from that unit

options.label: D
options.text: Willingness to pay for that unit

options.label: E
options.text: Share of total market surplus

explanation: Supply shows sellers' minimum acceptable prices or marginal costs. A market price above those amounts creates producer surplus.

prompt: Based on the figure below, consumer surplus at equilibrium is the area

options.label: A
options.text: Above supply and below Pe from zero to Qe

options.label: B
options.text: Below demand and below supply from zero to Qe

options.label: C
options.text: Between Pe and the quantity axis beyond Qe

options.label: D
options.text: Above demand and above Pe from zero to Qe

options.label: E
options.text: Below demand and above Pe from zero to Qe

explanation: For every purchased unit, subtract price from the demand curve's willingness to pay. Adding these differences gives the area below demand and above Pe through Qe.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity is on the horizontal axis. Demand D slopes downward and supply S slopes upward, intersecting at E with dashed guides to Pe and Qe. The region below D and above Pe between zero and Qe is shaded and labeled Area X.

graphScenes.caption: Schematic; only labeled numbers are quantitative

prompt: Total economic surplus in a market equals

options.label: A
options.text: The sum of all buyers’ willingness to pay

options.label: B
options.text: Equilibrium price multiplied by equilibrium quantity

options.label: C
options.text: Consumer surplus plus producer surplus

options.label: D
options.text: Consumer surplus minus producer surplus

options.label: E
options.text: Buyers’ total spending minus sellers’ total revenue

explanation: Total surplus adds buyers' and sellers' gains. It equals consumer surplus plus producer surplus.

prompt: A seller’s willingness to sell a unit is best represented by

options.label: A
options.text: The consumer surplus earned on the unit

options.label: B
options.text: The total revenue collected from all units

options.label: C
options.text: The minimum price that covers the seller’s cost

options.label: D
options.text: The equilibrium price received by every seller

options.label: E
options.text: The maximum price a buyer assigns to the unit

explanation: A seller requires a price sufficient to cover the unit's cost. That cost determines the minimum acceptable price.

prompt: At equilibrium, the marginal buyer is the buyer whose willingness to pay is

options.label: A
options.text: Equal to the market price

options.label: B
options.text: Equal to the marginal seller’s producer surplus

options.label: C
options.text: Greater than every other buyer’s valuation

options.label: D
options.text: Equal to total consumer surplus in the market

options.label: E
options.text: Less than the cost of the marginal unit

explanation: The marginal buyer values the last unit exactly at the market price. That buyer is indifferent between buying and not buying.

prompt: At equilibrium, the marginal seller is the seller whose cost is

options.label: A
options.text: Equal to the market price

options.label: B
options.text: Greater than the marginal buyer’s valuation

options.label: C
options.text: Equal to total producer surplus in the market

options.label: D
options.text: Equal to the demand curve’s price intercept

options.label: E
options.text: Lower than every other seller’s cost

explanation: The marginal seller's cost equals the market price. Supplying that marginal unit creates no extra producer surplus.

prompt: Which of the following best explains the information conveyed by an equilibrium price?

options.label: A
options.text: It guides buyers’ and sellers’ resource-allocation decisions

options.label: B
options.text: It fixes the quantity each consumer must purchase

options.label: C
options.text: It guarantees equal surplus for every market participant

options.label: D
options.text: It eliminates differences in production costs among firms

options.label: E
options.text: It makes buyers’ valuations identical to sellers’ costs

explanation: Market price conveys information about buyers' valuations and resource scarcity. Participants use it to decide what to purchase and produce.

prompt: A voluntary purchase generates positive consumer surplus when

options.label: A
options.text: The market quantity exceeds the equilibrium quantity

options.label: B
options.text: The seller’s cost exceeds the price received

options.label: C
options.text: The buyer’s willingness to pay exceeds the price

options.label: D
options.text: The price exceeds the buyer’s willingness to pay

options.label: E
options.text: The buyer’s valuation equals the seller’s revenue

explanation: When willingness to pay exceeds the price, the buyer receives a positive net benefit. The difference is consumer surplus.

prompt: Based on the figure below, producer surplus at equilibrium is represented by

options.label: A
options.text: Area X, below demand and above Pe through Qe

options.label: B
options.text: Area Y, above supply and below Pe through Qe

options.label: C
options.text: Area X plus Area Y only above the demand curve

options.label: D
options.text: The rectangle with height Pe and width Qe

options.label: E
options.text: Area Z, above demand and below supply beyond Qe

explanation: Area Y lies above supply and below Pe for the units sold. It adds the price-minus-cost gains of sellers and is producer surplus.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity is on the horizontal axis. Demand D slopes downward and supply S slopes upward, intersecting at E with guides to Pe and Qe. The region above S and below Pe through Qe is shaded and labeled Area Y; the region above Pe and below D is labeled Area X.

prompt: The area of a triangular consumer-surplus region is calculated as

options.label: A
options.text: Its price height divided by its quantity base

options.label: B
options.text: Its quantity base times its price height

options.label: C
options.text: One-half times its price base plus its quantity height

options.label: D
options.text: Its quantity base divided by twice its price height

options.label: E
options.text: One-half times its quantity base times its price height

explanation: A triangular surplus region has area one-half its quantity base times its price height.

prompt: In the absence of market failures, competitive equilibrium is efficient because it

options.label: A
options.text: Requires every seller to have the same cost

options.label: B
options.text: Maximizes consumer surplus plus producer surplus

options.label: C
options.text: Allocates every unit to the lowest-value buyer

options.label: D
options.text: Maximizes the market price received by sellers

options.label: E
options.text: Makes consumer surplus equal producer surplus

explanation: Without market failures, competitive equilibrium includes all trades whose benefits exceed costs. This maximizes total surplus.

prompt: Which transaction adds to total surplus?

options.label: A
options.text: A unit for which the seller’s cost exceeds the buyer’s willingness to pay

options.label: B
options.text: A unit for which price exceeds both valuation and cost

options.label: C
options.text: A unit for which the buyer’s willingness to pay exceeds the seller’s cost

options.label: D
options.text: A unit for which cost equals total market revenue

options.label: E
options.text: A unit for which the buyer’s willingness to pay equals zero

explanation: A trade adds surplus when the buyer's value exceeds the unit's production cost. The gain equals willingness to pay minus cost.

explanation: The buyer's surplus is $18 - $13 = $5.
